title: Gus and Mabel's Dream Ribbon
markdown:
Gus the goose gosling had played all day in the warm sun, chasing butterflies and splashing in puddles. Now, as the evening air grew soft and cool, he felt sleepy. He snuggled close beside Mabel the moon bunny. Gus was all fluffy and warm. He felt a little wiggle in his fluffy pocket.

“Oh my,” whispered Gus. His voice was like a soft breeze in the tall meadow grass. “I have Mabel’s special dream ribbon right here in my pocket.”

Mabel’s moonbeam eyes blinked. Her long ears twitched ever so softly. “My dream ribbon?” Her voice was a petal falling from a sleepy flower.

“Yes,” Gus honked ever so softly, the gentlest sigh. “I borrowed it for a little while. I wanted to peek at the sparkly wonderful dreams inside. But now it’s time to take it back home. It belongs in your lovely cozy burrow.”

Softly, softly, home we go.

So Gus and Mabel decided to go on a little adventure. A very quiet adventure.

“Let’s go, Mabel,” said Gus. He waddled along. His little webbed feet made soft rustling sounds on the dew-kissed grass. Mabel hopped gently beside him. Her long ears swayed like sleepy willow branches. The meadow was bathed in a soft silver light from the moon above. Little crickets chirped a sweet lullaby. The pretty meadow flowers were tucking themselves in, closing their petals for a long good night’s sleep.

“Oh look, Gus,” whispered Mabel. She pointed a tiny soft paw toward the sky. “The stars are like tiny twinkly diamonds.” They were scattered all across a dark blue velvet blanket.

Gus tilted his fluffy head and looked up. He saw the big moon, round and soft like a giant milky pearl, smiling down with a gentle sleepy smile. It was all so peaceful. So quiet. Wonderfully lovely.

They didn’t hurry along at all. The whole world felt safe and warm and just right. They ambled at their own sweet pace. The tall blades of grass tickled Gus’s tummy ever so slightly. Mabel’s whiskers twitched with delight.

Softly, softly, home we go.

Soon, through the soft moonlight, they saw the little familiar mounds of the rabbit burrow, nestled snugly into the earth. “There it is,” honked Gus, a tiny warm hug in his voice.

Mabel nudged him softly with her velvety nose. Together they were very, very careful. They placed the shimmering delicate dream ribbon right at the entrance of the burrow. It shone with its own soft light, waiting. Gus and Mabel felt a lovely warm fuzzy feeling deep in their hearts, like a tiny happy sunbeam. They knew they had done a good deed.

“We did it, Mabel,” whispered Gus. A wave of sleepiness made his eyes feel heavy.

“Yes, Gus,” whispered Mabel. Her long ears drooped a little. Tired and happy. “It was a good day. And a good deed, too.”

Softly, softly, home we go.

And so the two little friends, feeling wonderfully cozy and perfectly content, turned back toward their own warm nests for a lovely night’s rest. The moonlight was like a soft warm hug wrapping around them. The quiet night was filled with gentle peaceful sounds. Gus nestled down deep in his cozy soft spot. Mabel curled up tight in her soft warm burrow. Soon their eyes grew heavy, like little curtains slowly closing. They drifted off to sleep, safe and sound, dreaming the sweetest most gentle dreams.
characters: Gus (a goose gosling), Mabel (a moon bunny)
